title: The system: a food-delivery checkout that charges exactly once
caption: The key is born on the phone, claimed in the payments DB, passed on to the card processor, and every event downstream carries an id that consumers dedup on.

steps.text: The guest taps Pay. The app creates one UUID for this checkout and stores it, so every retry, even after the app restarts, sends the same Idempotency-Key.
The payment service inserts the key with status in_progress and a hash of the request. The unique index lets exactly one attempt win the claim.
The winner charges the card and passes a key derived from the same one, so the processor also refuses a second charge.
One local transaction writes the payment, marks the key done with the stored response, and adds an outbox row. The 201 goes back to the app.
The outbox relay publishes PaymentSucceeded. The stream promises at-least-once delivery, so duplicates are normal.
Each consumer dedups on event_id: points are added and the id recorded in one transaction; the receipt email is keyed by payment id.

scenarios.name: Dinner rush
scenarios.summary: Mobile networks drop 2% of replies at peak: retries become steady traffic, and the key turns them into cheap reads.

steps.text: 20 000 checkouts a minute; 400 of them never see their reply and retry with backoff and jitter.
A retry that finds the key done gets the stored response straight from the DB: no charge, ~2 ms.
A retry that arrives while the first attempt is still charging finds in_progress and gets 409 with Retry-After.
The processor sees one charge per checkout; the reconciler finds nothing to fix.

scenarios.name: Relay publishes twice
scenarios.summary: The relay crashes after publishing but before marking the outbox row sent: the event goes out again, and the consumers absorb it.

steps.text: The relay publishes PaymentSucceeded for pay_42.
It dies before recording that the row was sent.
A new relay instance reads the same unsent row and publishes pay_42 again.
Loyalty points tries to insert event_id into its seen table; the conflict means skip. Points are added once.
The receipt sender checks 'already sent for pay_42' and stays quiet.

scenarios.name: Retention cut
scenarios.summary: To save storage, someone shortens key retention from 7 days to 1 hour. An app that retries later is no longer recognised.

steps.text: A cleanup change deletes key rows older than 1 hour.
A phone that lost signal on a train comes back 3 hours later and retries the stored request with its key.
The key looks new, the claim succeeds, and only the processor's own dedup window (or nothing) stands between the guest and a second charge.
Mitigation: retention longer than the longest client retry horizon, plus a UNIQUE(order_id) on payments as a second referee.
